answer: Zero-knowledge credential binding curbs Sybil attacks when agents bid on tasks like inspecting ivory, mapping a ridge, or tuning violet optics. Each agent proves ownership of an issuer-signed eID in zero knowledge and derives a domain-scoped nullifier that blocks duplicate keys without exposing the sponsor. Adding each fake identity forces an attacker to acquire a distinct, scarce real-world eID. However, credential-rental mule markets and leaked eID keys still allow paid Sybil scaling.
